## Findings
- claim-1: The inspected paper states that for \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the ideal \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is generated by each of \[ \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},\qquad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}. \] [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892]
- claim-2: In the inclusion special case \(t=r\) or \(t=s\), the paper compares its second family with the generators of Gasharov–Reiner (GR02); for \(t=s\), it has \(i=b=1\), \(j=r-s+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-1,s-1)\), and obtains the first \(\min(n-r,s)\) GR02 generators. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 893-933]
- claim-3: The omitted semantic remark is: “the techniques utilized in [GR02] seem very particular to the case where \(X_w\) is defined by inclusions. We do not know how to use them for some alternate approach to the case of general \(X_w\) considered in this paper.” [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 934-937]
- claim-4: GR02 is repeatedly referenced: as prior \(n^2\)-generator work for Schubert varieties defined by inclusions (including smooth ones), in the essential-set discussion, in the comparison above, and in the final open question; its bibliography entry is V. Gasharov and V. Reiner, *Cohomology of smooth Schubert varieties in partial flag manifolds*, JLMS 66 (2002), 550–562. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 67-106]
- claim-5: The paper formally conjectures minimality of both displayed \(J_v\)-families and records only a finite computer verification for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-946]
## Strategy
Use the inspected full text of Reiner–Woo–Yong (2011) to identify Theorem 4.8’s integral \(J_v\)-families, its GR02 inclusion-case comparison, repeated GR02 references, and the omitted lines 934–937 remark. The requested source-30 extraction target is established.

## Gaps
No gap for this bounded extraction. GR02 itself was not independently inspected; no claim is made about methods beyond the inspected source.
